title: Trio ID'd After Fatal Head-On Molly Pitcher Highway Crash In Franklin County: PA State Police - NewsBreak
text:
By Jillian Pikora ,
6 hours ago
Three people were killed early Wednesday, Nov. 5 in a head-on collision along Route 11, also known as Molly Pitcher Highway, in Greene Township, Franklin County, Pennsylvania State Police said.
The crash happened at 6545 Molly Pitcher Highway (State Route 11) around 6:31 a.m., according to the Pennsylvania State Police–Chambersburg. A 2006 Lincoln Zephyr driven by 47-year-old Saintanie Jean Baptiste of Chambersburg was traveling southbound when it crossed the center turning lane and entered the northbound lane, striking a 2010 Peterbilt 386 tractor-trailer head-on.
Jean Baptiste and two passengers—42-year-old Jodelens Joseph of Chambersburg and 30-year-old Claire M. Elveus of Lauderhill, Florida—were all pronounced dead at the scene. Police confirmed that Jean Baptiste and Joseph were wearing lap and shoulder belts, while Elveus was not.
The tractor-trailer driver, identified in the report as Dandre L. Hayes, 36, of Pennsylvania, was wearing a seatbelt and sustained a possible injury but was not transported for treatment.
The Lincoln came to rest in the center turning lane facing west, while the tractor-trailer ended up off the east shoulder of the road facing north. Both vehicles were towed from the scene—Rife Motors handled the Zephyr and Dave’s Truck Repair towed the Peterbilt.
Emergency responders from West End Fire Company 15, Pleasant Hall EMS, Chambersburg EMS, and WellSpan EMS assisted at the crash site.
Route 11 was closed for several hours but later reopened late Wednesday morning. The cause of the crash remains under investigation by PSP Chambersburg.
